answer: Named-window pulse ledger: each identity must emit a signed pulse at a random slot inside every window, and the ledger records arrival delta from the slot center. Missing a pulse or drifting past the tolerance marks the identity suspect until it proves it holds the same secret key under a fresh random challenge. Automating many identities means sustaining independent timing across a gale of windows, since each clone needs its own clock discipline and challenge responses, multiplying per-unit operational cost and exposing synchronized duplicates.
